territory: App shell, layouts, client chrome, telemetry plumbing: src/app/layout.tsx, (main)/layout.tsx + template/error/not-found, src/components/layout/** (sidebar, notification-bell, app-shell, page-header, content-column, search-pill, konami-eggs, logo-fact, rail-grid), src/components/common/** (motion, image-viewer, bird-avatar pair, buttons, typeahead hooks), src/components/tour/** + src/lib/tour-*, theme plumbing + /dark-mode, /birds + /pick-bird, src/lib/wordle.ts, mascot flight layer + sidebar hoopoe, proxy.ts header plumbing, last-seen/content-view/search-log telemetry, loading.tsx coverage across (main)

findings.title: Server-rendered dates show the UTC calendar day, not IST: every date between midnight and 05:30 IST renders one day early
findings.expected: A letter posted at 00:30 IST on 15 July shows "15 July" everywhere; all absolute dates agree across surfaces for the IST-based membership.
findings.actual: Server components format dates with the server's timezone (UTC on Vercel). Any timestamp between 18:30 and 23:59 UTC — i.e. anything a member does between midnight and 05:30 IST, a prime posting window — renders as the previous day on every server-rendered surface. Worse, the SAME timestamp renders differently on different surfaces: post-card.tsx and collection-client.tsx are "use client" (browser = IST, correct day) while the letters index, the letter reader byline, and the admin tables are server components (UTC, wrong day), so one letter can show "14 Jul" in the letters index and "15 Jul" on the feed card simultaneously.
findings.evidence: src/lib/utils.ts:151-157: `export function formatDisplayDate(date: Date | string): string { return new Date(date).toLocaleDateString("en-GB", { day: "numeric", month: "short", year: "numeric" }) }` — no `timeZone` option, so it resolves to the runtime's zone. Called from server components: letters/page.tsx:163 `metaLine(batchLine(l.author), formatDisplayDate(l.createdAt))`, letters/[id]/page.tsx:188 `date={formatDisplayDate(letter.createdAt)}`, admin/support/page.tsx:222, admin/catchups/page.tsx:136-138, admin/people/person-detail.tsx (multiple). The letter reader also inline-formats server-side at letters/[id]/page.tsx:165-169: `new Date(letter.createdAt).toLocaleDateString("en-GB", { day: "numeric", month: "long", year: "numeric" })` — again no timeZone. Meanwhile src/components/posts/post-card.tsx:1 is `"use client"` and calls `formatDisplayDate(post.createdAt)` at line 108 in the browser (IST for members), proving the cross-surface disagreement. `formatTimeAgo`'s >4-week fallback (utils.ts:21) has the same gap but runs client-side in the bell, so it is mostly unaffected. Vercel servers run UTC; members are IST (+5:30) — the brief's exact 6h class.
findings.fixDirection: Add `timeZone: "Asia/Kolkata"` to formatDisplayDate and to the inline toLocaleDateString calls in server components (letters/[id]/page.tsx:165, and audit every server-side toLocaleDateString/toLocaleString in src/app and src/components without a "use client" directive). The site's audience is IST by definition (same rule wordle.ts:18-21 already applies with `istDateKey` using `timeZone: "Asia/Kolkata"` — follow that precedent). Alternatively move date formatting into client components, but the one-line timeZone option is smaller and keeps RSC rendering.
findings.gateOrTest: New unit test beside the existing 14 (npm run check): assert formatDisplayDate(new Date("2026-07-14T19:00:00Z")) === "15 Jul 2026" (19:00 UTC = 00:30 IST next day). It fails today, passes after the fix.
findings.reproPlan: Read-only: in chrome-devtools, load /letters signed in and evaluate the rendered byline for any letter whose createdAt falls in the 18:30-24:00 UTC window (query not needed — compare the same letter's date on /feed vs /letters).

findings.title: NotificationBell: three unguarded server-action awaits — a single transient failure permanently kills infinite scroll, makes notification clicks silently do nothing, or wedges "Loading..."
findings.expected: A failed fetch of the next notifications page retries on the next scroll; clicking a notification always navigates to its target; a failed first-page load shows something actionable.
findings.actual: (1) handleLoadMore sets loadingMoreRef.current = true, awaits getNotifications, and only resets the flag on the success path — no try/finally. One rejection (flaky mobile network, DB hiccup) leaves the flag true forever: every later sentinel intersection returns at the `if (loadingMoreRef.current || !hasMore) return;` guard, the skeleton shimmer row stays visible, and the list can never load more until a full page reload. (2) handleClickNotification does `await markNotificationRead(notif.id)` BEFORE `router.push(notif.link)`; if the action rejects, the push never runs — the member taps a notification and nothing happens, no toast, just an unhandled rejection in the console. This rejection is not only network: `prisma.notification.update({ where: { id, userId } })` (actions.ts:77-80) throws P2025 when the row is gone — e.g. a tab holding rows past position 100 while another first-page open ran the KEEP=100 prune (actions.ts:44-57 deletes everything older than the 100th-newest). Even on success, navigation is serialized behind a full server-action round trip to Mumbai, so every notification tap pays extra latency for a bookkeeping write. (3) handleOpen has no catch: a rejection leaves loaded=false and the panel shows "Loading..." until closed and reopened.
findings.evidence: notification-bell.tsx:147-158: `async function handleLoadMore() { if (loadingMoreRef.current || !hasMore) return; loadingMoreRef.current = true; const data = await getNotifications({ cursor: nextCursor }); ... loadingMoreRef.current = false; }` — the reset is unreachable on throw. Lines 160-171: `if (!notif.read) { await markNotificationRead(notif.id); ... } if (notif.link) { router.push(notif.link); }`. Lines 134-145 handleOpen: `const data = await getNotifications(); setNotifications(...); setLoaded(true);` with `void handleOpen()` at line 121 — rejection is unhandled. actions.ts:77-80: `await prisma.notification.update({ where: { id: notificationId, userId: session.user.id }, data: { read: true } })` — Prisma update throws P2025 on zero matching rows; there is no P2002/P2025 handling anywhere in the file.
findings.fixDirection: handleLoadMore: wrap in try/finally so loadingMoreRef always resets. handleClickNotification: navigate first (or in parallel) and mark-read optimistically — `router.push` should not be gated on the write; catch the action failure and revert the optimistic decrement (or just toast). markNotificationRead server-side: use updateMany (no-throw on zero rows) instead of update, keeping the userId scope. handleOpen: catch, and render a small "Couldn't load — tap to retry" row instead of eternal "Loading...".
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test for the actions file: markNotificationRead with a non-existent id resolves (updateMany) rather than throwing. For the client, a component test simulating a rejected getNotifications and asserting a second load attempt still fires is the pin; at minimum the try/finally is trivially inspectable in /check's tsc pass.
findings.reproPlan: Read-only-ish: in chrome-devtools, open the bell, use network emulation (offline) mid-scroll of the panel, restore network, observe the sentinel shimmer never resolves; click an unread notification while offline and observe no navigation and no error surface.

findings.title: Unread badge can only ever fall, never rise: initialUnreadCount is captured once into state with no prop re-sync, making the bell's shake-on-new-notification animation unreachable dead code and the badge stale for the whole session
findings.expected: The bell badge reflects arriving notifications during a session (the shake effect at lines 109-115 exists specifically to fire "when the unread count RISES"), and the count shown after navigation matches what the member just did in the panel.
findings.actual: `const [unreadCount, setUnreadCount] = useState(initialUnreadCount)` (line 98) never re-syncs when the prop later changes, and the only setUnreadCount calls are `Math.max(0, c - 1)` (line 166) and `setUnreadCount(0)` (line 176) — both decrements. So within any mounted bell instance the count monotonically falls: (a) notifications arriving during a session never surface on the badge (the header-variant dot at line 205 renders only when unreadCount > 0, so a member browsing all day sees no indicator at all until a hard reload, even though opening the panel would show unread rows); (b) the shake effect (lines 109-115, `if (unreadCount > prevUnread.current) setShakeKey(...)`) can never fire — confirmed dead code, which is strong evidence the prop was expected to flow through; (c) two bell instances don't share state: on mobile, mark-all-read in /feed's header bell (its own instance) then navigating to /letters mounts the sidebar band bell fresh from the Sidebar's `unreadCount` prop (sidebar.tsx:740), which is whatever the (main) layout last rendered — under App Router partial rendering the shared layout is not re-executed on soft navigation, so the cleared badge can resurrect with the pre-read count until a refetch that includes the layout happens.
findings.evidence: notification-bell.tsx:97-98: `const [notifications, setNotifications] = useState<Notification[]>([]); const [unreadCount, setUnreadCount] = useState(initialUnreadCount);` — no useEffect or render-adjust syncing from initialUnreadCount afterwards. Lines 109-115: `useEffect(() => { if (unreadCount > prevUnread.current) { setShakeKey((k) => k + 1); } prevUnread.current = unreadCount; }, [unreadCount]);` — grep confirms setUnreadCount appears only at lines 166 (`setUnreadCount((c) => Math.max(0, c - 1))`) and 176 (`setUnreadCount(0)`); nothing ever increases it. handleOpen (134-145) refreshes the LIST every open but never recomputes unreadCount from the fresh data, so badge and list visibly disagree after another device/tab reads or receives notifications. markAllNotificationsRead's `revalidatePath("/")` (actions.ts:95) targets only the root page path, not the layout, so it does not push a corrected count either.
findings.fixDirection: Three coordinated small changes: (1) sync state to the prop with the sanctioned adjust-during-render pattern (track prevInitial; when initialUnreadCount changes, setUnreadCount to it) — this also resurrects the shake; (2) have getNotifications return the fresh unread total and set it in handleOpen so badge and list always agree; (3) use `revalidatePath("/", "layout")` (or a targeted tag) in the two mark-read actions so the layout's count refetches. A later polling/refresh mechanism is optional; these three make the existing plumbing self-consistent.
findings.gateOrTest: The tour-provider-style .test.mjs harness can pin the pure part: extracting the shake-decision into a function tested for the rising case. Live pin: e2e spec asserting the badge equals the panel's unread rows after open.
findings.reproPlan: Live: sign in as admin in chrome-devtools with 0 unread; from a second session trigger a like on the admin's post; navigate between pages in tab 1 — badge stays absent; open the panel — unread row is there, badge still absent. Mobile-width repro of the resurrection: mark all read via /feed header bell, navigate to /letters, read the band bell badge.

findings.title: Fire-and-forget DB writes in server components without after(): recordView (4 pages) and logSearch (feed) can be killed by serverless suspend, silently losing the analytics they exist to record
findings.expected: View counters and search logs are recorded reliably — either awaited off the critical path or scheduled via after()/waitUntil, the pattern this codebase itself already established (drainMailQueue runs inside after() in (main)/layout.tsx:63 precisely because "it must run AFTER the response"; touchLastSeen is awaited inside the layout's Promise.all).
findings.actual: `void recordView(session.user.id, "letter", letter.id)` (letters/[id]/page.tsx:85, and the same shape at collection/[id]/page.tsx:58, profile/[id]/page.tsx:117, catchups/round/[editionId]/page.tsx:194) and `void logSearch({ scope: "feed", query: q, userId })` (feed/page.tsx:31) detach a Postgres round trip from the render. On Vercel the function may be suspended as soon as the response finishes streaming; a detached promise that has not yet resolved is not guaranteed to run. The writes therefore succeed or vanish depending on timing — the owner's "most viewed" analytics and search log undercount non-deterministically, and because recordView/logSearch swallow errors in production (content-view.ts:34-38, search-log.ts) there is no signal it is happening.
findings.evidence: letters/[id]/page.tsx:85: `void recordView(session.user.id, "letter", letter.id);` — inside the RSC render, no after(). content-view.ts:28-33 shows it is a real network write: `await prisma.contentView.upsert({...})`. feed/page.tsx:29-31: `if (q) { const s = await auth(); void logSearch({ scope: "feed", query: q, userId: s?.user?.id }); }`. Contrast with the codebase's own correct pattern, (main)/layout.tsx:63-69: `after(async () => { try { await drainMailQueue(); } catch (err) {...} });` with the comment explaining post-response work must use after(). The four recordView call sites and the feed logSearch call are the only detached DB writes in server components (grep verified).
findings.fixDirection: Wrap each in `after(() => recordView(...))` / `after(() => logSearch(...))` (import from next/server, already used in the same tree), preserving the never-throws contract inside. Do not await them serially in render — the point of the current shape (not delaying the page) is right; only the scheduling primitive is wrong.
findings.gateOrTest: grep-style regression check in the security-regressions/unit test suite: assert no `void recordView(`/`void logSearch(` outside an after() callback (a simple source scan test in the existing .mjs test pattern).
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only (the loss is a serverless-runtime timing property; locally the dev server never suspends, so it cannot be demonstrated read-only).

findings.title: One error boundary for the whole app: any thrown error in any (main) widget or page unmounts the entire shell (sidebar, nav, bell) into a bare full-screen error; no route-group error.tsx, no global-error.tsx
findings.expected: An error in one page or one widget (e.g. FeedRail's query failing) degrades that region: the shell and navigation survive, and the member can move to another page. The taxonomy's question — "one thrown error in a widget: does the whole shell die?" — should answer no.
findings.actual: find over src/app returns exactly one error boundary: src/app/error.tsx. There is no error.tsx in (main), (auth), admin, or any nested segment, and there are no <ErrorBoundary>-style client boundaries around widgets (FeedRail, the notification panel, etc.). So a render-time throw anywhere under (main) — a page's Prisma query rejecting after the shell streamed, a widget's bad data — replaces EVERYTHING including the sidebar with the root boundary's full-screen `min-h-screen` card (error.tsx:16). The member loses navigation entirely; their only affordance is "Try again" re-running the same failing tree. Separately, there is no global-error.tsx, so an error thrown by the root layout itself falls through to Next's unstyled default page (low likelihood today — the root layout only awaits getThemeCookie — but zero-cost to cover).
findings.evidence: find output (verified): error boundaries = `src/app/error.tsx` only, against ~46 (main) pages. error.tsx:16: `<div className="flex min-h-screen flex-col items-center justify-center bg-background px-4 text-center">` — a viewport-filling replacement, no shell. (main)/layout.tsx:35-41 throws to this same boundary if the notification count query rejects (DB down), which is acceptable for a layout-level failure, but page-level failures (e.g. letters/[id] canViewCityScope query rejecting at line 106 of that page) take the shell down with them for no reason.
findings.fixDirection: Add src/app/(main)/error.tsx rendering the same copy inside the content column — because it sits below (main)/layout.tsx, the AppShell/sidebar stay mounted and the member keeps navigation. Optionally one more in admin. Add a minimal global-error.tsx (own <html><body>) for root-layout failures. Widget-level boundaries (FeedRail) are a nice-to-have after that.
findings.gateOrTest: e2e: a lab-only route that throws on demand, asserting `aside` (the sidebar rail) is still present when the error card shows. Simpler pin: the lab registry audit could assert (main)/error.tsx exists.
findings.reproPlan: Live-safe: temporarily unreachable read-only — instead verify by navigating to a route and using next-devtools get_errors after inducing a client-side throw in a widget via evaluate_script (React DevTools error injection); or accept the structural argument (single boundary file is a fact of the tree).

findings.title: Five async DB-backed routes ship no loading.tsx, so navigating to them gives zero feedback for the full auth+DB round trip — including the letter reader, the app's core reading surface
findings.expected: House rule (CLAUDE.md): "Any new async route ships a loading.tsx using the warm shimmer." Clicking a letter shows the shimmer immediately while the server renders.
findings.actual: find over src/app shows loading.tsx everywhere EXCEPT these async pages: letters/[id] (page runs auth + post.findUnique + optional groupMember.findUnique + canViewCityScope, all sequential — lines 66-106 — plus generateMetadata's own duplicate set), collection/[id] (auth + photo.findUnique in both generateMetadata and page), notice/[id] (auth + notification.findUnique), support (auth + contribution aggregates), admin/audit (prisma queries; every OTHER admin section has loading.tsx — audit is the one omission). Without a loading boundary the App Router keeps the old page on screen with no indicator until the new page's RSC fully resolves: on a cold serverless start + Mumbai DB round trips, a member taps a letter in the index and the UI is frozen-looking for the whole wait. Sibling routes prove the standard: letters/, letters/new, letters/[id]/edit all HAVE loading.tsx — the reader itself is the gap.
findings.evidence: find output: loading.tsx exists for 29 routes; absent for the five above. letters/[id]/page.tsx:66-106 chains `await auth()` → `await prisma.post.findUnique({... include: {author, _count, likes, bookmarks}})` → (group letters) `await prisma.groupMember.findUnique(...)` → `await canViewCityScope(...)` — three-plus sequential round trips before any byte of UI. collection/[id]/page.tsx:22 `const photo = await prisma.photo.findUnique(` inside generateMetadata plus the page's own fetch. admin/ has loading.tsx for analytics, catchups, content, mail, messages, people, reports, support — but not audit.
findings.fixDirection: Add loading.tsx with the warm shimmer for letters/[id], collection/[id], notice/[id], support, and admin/audit, matching the skeleton pattern the sibling routes already use (letters/loading.tsx and collection/loading.tsx are ready templates). While there, letters/[id] could parallelize the groupMember + cityScope checks after the letter fetch, but the loading boundary is the member-visible fix.
findings.gateOrTest: The repo's lab-registry-style audit could add a check: every page.tsx that imports prisma has a loading.tsx in its segment or an ancestor below the route group. Otherwise: visual suite already covers letters index; add /letters/[id] to ROUTES in e2e/visual.spec.ts when fixed.
findings.reproPlan: Live read-only: chrome-devtools with network throttling (Slow 3G), click a letter from /letters, observe no UI change until the full response lands.

findings.title: MascotFlightLayer: a second launch while a flight is live shares abortRef/rafRef/ranId with the first — the first flight's failsafe then aborts and unmounts the second mid-air, deleting the bird in front of the viewer
findings.expected: Launching a new flight cancels the previous one cleanly; only one runFlight loop ever drives the portal.
findings.actual: onLaunch → `setActive({ ...launch, id: Date.now() })` (line 203) remounts the Hoopoe (key change) and queues a new runFlight, but NOTHING cancels the previous runFlight: its rAF chain keeps stepping (it holds its own closure; the shared `rafRef` only tracks the newest frame id), and because the old rig was stopped at remount, its awaited rig verbs (`await api.perch()`, line 493) never settle — motion v12's .stop() never resolves .finished (documented in this very file's comments, lines 195-201). Flight 1 therefore hangs until ITS failsafe (line 292-297) fires, which sets the SHARED `abortRef.current = true`, cancels the SHARED rafRef (flight 2's current frame), calls signalHandoff, and `setActive(null)` — unmounting the portal while flight 2 is mid-cruise. The visible result is the second bird vanishing abruptly mid-air. Entry path: the landing's own double-click is guarded (`if (phase === "exiting") return`, landing-hero.tsx:211), but browser-Back to the landing during the first flight's 2.5s no-perch hover window (destination never mounted because the user backed out) and clicking the other CTA reproduces it within the 5.8s failsafe window.
findings.evidence: Line 203: `return onLaunch((launch) => setActive({ ...launch, id: Date.now() }));` — no cancellation of a live flight. Lines 258-261: `async function runFlight(api, flight) { if (ranId.current === flight.id) return; ranId.current = flight.id; abortRef.current = false;` — flight 2 resets the shared abort flag while flight 1 still reads it. Lines 292-297 (flight 1's failsafe, still armed): `abortRef.current = true; signalHandoff(); cancelAnimationFrame(rafRef.current); setActive(null);` — rafRef at that moment holds flight 2's frame id, and setActive(null) removes flight 2's portal. Flight 1's `finally` (573-577) also does `cancelAnimationFrame(rafRef.current)`.
findings.fixDirection: Give each runFlight its own abort token (the not-found.tsx flight-token pattern in the same codebase is the worked example) instead of the shared refs, and have the onLaunch handler cancel the current token before setActive; clear the previous failsafe on new launch. Alternatively, ignore launches while active is non-null (one flight at a time is already the bus's stated contract, mascot-flight.ts:15-18).
findings.gateOrTest: scripts/qa/hoopoe-landing-check.mjs already samples the flyer's transform per frame; extend it with a back-nav + second-CTA scenario asserting the [data-mascot-flyer] element survives to handoff.
findings.reproPlan: Live: chrome-devtools on the landing at desktop width — click Sign in, immediately history.back(), click Join within ~3s, watch the second bird vanish when the first flight's 5.8s failsafe fires.

findings.title: generateMetadata re-runs the page's full permission-checked fetch with no React cache(), doubling DB round trips (up to 6 queries per letter view)
findings.expected: Next's documented pattern for fetch-in-metadata is to share the lookup via React cache() so metadata and page cost one query set.
findings.actual: letters/[id] runs post.findUnique + (group) groupMember.findUnique + canViewCityScope in generateMetadata (lines 24-56) and then the same three again in the page body (lines 69-106) — Prisma calls are not deduplicated by the framework (only fetch() is). collection/[id] has the same shape (photo.findUnique in both). Every letter view costs 4-6 DB round trips where 2-3 suffice; at 2,000 users this is not a stability risk, but it is doubled latency exposure on the two heaviest read pages and doubled pgbouncer connection churn for nothing.
findings.evidence: letters/[id]/page.tsx:24: `const letter = await prisma.post.findUnique({ where: { id }, select: { title, content, kind, isHidden, groupId, cityScope, status, authorId } })` inside generateMetadata; page.tsx:69: `const letter = await prisma.post.findUnique({ where: { id }, include: { author..., _count..., likes..., bookmarks... } })` — two independent queries for the same row, plus the duplicated groupMember (47 and 97) and canViewCityScope (55 and 106) checks.
findings.fixDirection: Wrap a shared `getLetterForViewer(id, userId)` in React `cache()` (from "react") returning the row plus the visibility verdict; call it from both generateMetadata and the page. Same for collection/[id]'s photo lookup.
findings.gateOrTest: Prisma query logging in dev (get_logs via next-devtools) before/after: one findUnique per view instead of two.
findings.reproPlan: Live read-only: enable Prisma query logging on the dev server, load a letter, count the duplicate SELECTs in the log.

findings.title: AppShell reserves 64px of bottom padding on mobile for a "fixed bottom tab bar" that does not exist on the real site
findings.expected: Mobile pages end where their content ends (plus safe-area padding); a padding reservation exists only for chrome that is actually rendered.
findings.actual: app-shell.tsx:58-59: `{/* pb on mobile clears the fixed bottom tab bar */}` above `<div className="relative z-10 flex min-w-0 flex-1 flex-col pb-16 md:pb-0">`. A repo-wide search finds no fixed bottom tab bar anywhere in the app (the only fixed-bottom elements are the tour panel/offer, which are transient overlays, and the demo-only DemoBar — which sits at `bottom-20` on mobile, i.e. it is itself positioned ABOVE this phantom 64px reservation). On the production site every mobile page therefore carries 64px of dead space below its content — visible as an oversized gap under the last card on every scroll-to-bottom, on every page. The comment describes chrome that was evidently removed (the drawer Sheet replaced it) without the padding following.
findings.evidence: grep for fixed bottom bars across src (excluding lab): only tour-offer.tsx:52, tour-panel.tsx:86 (both transient z-[65] overlays), landing ambient-leaves (signed-out page), and demo-bar.tsx:82 `"pointer-events-none fixed right-4 bottom-20 z-50 ..."` (renders only when IS_DEMO, layout.tsx:120 `{IS_DEMO && <DemoBar userId={session.user.id} />}`). No tab bar component exists; sidebar.tsx's mobile chrome is a TOP band (line 641) plus a Sheet drawer.
findings.fixDirection: Either delete pb-16 (and let the demo add its own clearance, since DemoBar is the only bottom-floating chrome and it already floats at bottom-20), or reduce it to safe-area padding: `pb-[env(safe-area-inset-bottom)] md:pb-0`. Verify at 390x844 per the house mobile rule.
findings.gateOrTest: npm run visual at mobile viewport will catch the reflow — run visual:update after confirming the intentional change.
findings.reproPlan: Live: chrome-devtools resize_page to 390x844 on /feed, scroll to bottom, measure the gap below the last card (evaluate_script on the content wrapper's padding-bottom = 64px).

findings.title: ImageViewer's Download button silently degrades to open-in-new-tab in production because the R2 public host fetch is cross-origin and bucket CORS was never configured
findings.expected: "Download photo" saves the file, on the deployment members actually use.
findings.actual: download() does `const res = await fetch(current.src)` (line 184) — in production current.src is a `pub-*.r2.dev` URL, so this is a cross-origin fetch that requires CORS headers on the bucket. Project memory records the R2 bucket CORS configuration as blocked/never applied (the presign work hit the same wall). Without it, fetch rejects every time and the catch (line 192-194) falls back to `window.open(current.src, "_blank", "noopener,noreferrer")` — a new tab showing the image, which on iOS Safari especially is a confusing dead-end compared to a save. In local dev images are same-origin (/uploads), so the button works there and the degradation is invisible to development. Note also that even the anchor-download fallback path cannot work cross-origin (the download attribute is ignored for cross-origin URLs), so the new-tab behavior is total in prod until CORS is set.
findings.evidence: image-viewer.tsx:180-195: `async function download() { ... try { const res = await fetch(current.src); const blob = await res.blob(); ... a.download = name; a.click(); ... } catch { window.open(current.src, "_blank", "noopener,noreferrer"); } }`. AGENTS.md: images served from `pub-*.r2.dev`; storage.ts serves local filesystem in dev — so dev never exercises the cross-origin path. Suspected (not confirmed) because bucket CORS state is infrastructure, not code.
findings.fixDirection: Either configure R2 bucket CORS to allow GET from the site origin (also unblocks the tracked presign-upload work), or proxy the download through a small same-origin route (`/api/media/download?key=` streaming from R2 with Content-Disposition: attachment), which additionally fixes the filename and avoids exposing the r2.dev host. The in-code fallback is fine to keep.
findings.gateOrTest: After fix: an e2e step on the production URL clicking Download and asserting a download event rather than a popup (or a curl check that the pub URL answers with Access-Control-Allow-Origin).
findings.reproPlan: Live read-only on production: open any photo in the viewer, click Download, watch DevTools network for the CORS-failed fetch followed by the new tab.

findings.title: Mid-tour navigation leaves the spotlight measuring a detached element: the dim overlay collapses to a zero-rect pinhole at the viewport's top-left corner
findings.expected: If the spotlighted element disappears (the member clicks a sidebar link mid-tour — the overlay is pointer-events-none, so the whole app stays clickable), the spotlight falls back to the even full-page dim or clears.
findings.actual: The measuring effect's deps are [active, spotlightKey] (line 78). When the member navigates away mid-stop, the target unmounts and useTourAnchor's cleanup deregisters it (tour-anchors.ts:84-86), but neither `active` nor `spotlightKey` changed, so the effect never re-runs and its closure keeps the detached `el`. The ResizeObserver goes quiet, but the window scroll/resize listeners still call measure(): `el.getBoundingClientRect()` on a detached node returns all zeros, so setHole({left:0, top:0, width:0, height:0, radius:0}) — the box-shadow trick then paints the 55% ink dim over the ENTIRE viewport with a 2px leaf outline dot at (0,0). The member sees the new page uniformly dimmed with a stray green fleck top-left, with the tour card still docked; it only heals when they press Next/Skip.
findings.evidence: tour-spotlight.tsx:40-78: `useEffect(() => { ... const el = getSpotlightEl(spotlightKey); ... function measure() { const r = el!.getBoundingClientRect(); ... setHole({ left: r.left, top: r.top, width: r.width, height: r.height, radius }); } ... window.addEventListener("scroll", measure, { passive: true, capture: true }); ... }, [active, spotlightKey]);` — no re-check that el is still connected. tour-anchors.ts:84-86 cleanup: `return () => { if (getSpotlightEl(key) === el) clearSpotlight(key); }` removes it from the registry but cannot reach the spotlight's captured `el`. TourProvider keeps phase "running" across free navigation (no pathname watcher tears the stop down).
findings.fixDirection: In measure(), bail to setHole(null) when `!el.isConnected` (one line). Optionally, TourProvider could watch pathname while running and clear spotlightKey when the member navigates somewhere that is not the current stop's route.
findings.gateOrTest: tour-provider.test.mjs pattern: extract measure's rect-to-hole decision and test the zero-rect/disconnected case maps to null.
